unit_competencies.why: A week-long celebration with no written objectives (the four 'objectives' are one description repeated per band); if per-grade objectives are written, the hands-on experiments would evidence ncf.world.P.C-6.1 and C-7.1 (G3-G4) and ncf.fnd.F.C-7.2 (G1-G2).

A celebration (National Science Day), not a subject unit; its theme, India's contribution to science, is an NCF goal only from the middle stage (ncf.sci.M.C-8.1), with no preparatory or foundational equivalent.
A field visit (Science Park) with no written objectives; experiential exposure, not a competency of its own.
A field visit (Space Park) with no written objectives; experiential exposure, not a competency of its own.
A review-and-assessment slot at the end of the cooking strand, not a topic of its own; it re-tests the competencies of unit.092 to unit.102.

notes: The school's G3-G4 Science units (particles, energy transfers, Earth's structure, skeletons) are discipline-based, while NCF-SE 2023 gives the preparatory stage only World Around Us; their sole honest NCF homes are the familiarity rows ncf.world.P.C-7.1/C-7.2, so these units teach more content than NCF asks for at this stage and NCERT EVS 3-5 has no matching outcomes.

NCF has no vocational rows below the middle stage, so Home Science (stitching, weaving, cooking) is mapped to World Around Us (C-1.5 making objects, C-2.1/C-2.2 food and household systems, C-3.1 food safety, C-4.4 conserving resources) and foundational rows (C-1.1 nutritious food, C-1.4 safe tools, C-3.3 hand precision); a vocational target exists only from Grade 6.

Source defects: ncert.sci.6.04 and 6.05 are the same sentence (their targets were split across the three example investigations); unit.371 is a truncated duplicate of unit.322 ('and its Habitats'); unit.088-091 and unit.097-103 and unit.255-267 carry their objectives in the title field with empty samples.

NCERT's 2017/2019 outcomes give no evidence for several NCF rows, left with empty ncert lists: substance abuse (ncf.sci.M.C-4.4), open scientific questions (ncf.sci.M.C-9.2, ncf.sci.S.C-7.2), simple machines (ncf.sci.S.C-2.6), literature/arts and science (ncf.sci.S.C-5.1), science in music and dance (ncf.sci.S.C-5.3), and climate change or biodiversity collapse as such (ncf.env.S.C-1.1).

Environmental Education is graded G10 only (NCF-SE makes it a separate subject in Grade 10; its class 9 evidence is the interdependence outcome ncert.sci.9.17); five event units (Science Week, National Science Day, two field visits, Review and Assessment) are left without competencies with a 'why', since they have no written learning objectives.
